what_this_layer_is: The shape of what ships in git and is IMMUTABLE once tagged. A unit file is not the question bank — it is the bank's import source. Once imported, the database is authoritative and this file is provenance. Nothing that mutates after extraction belongs here; that is the RUNTIME layer.

companion_documents.runtime: runtime_schema_v1 — Query, Usage, Attempt, WeakItem, MarkResult, approval and revision lifecycle
companion_documents.procedure: extraction_procedure_v2 — how to read a source and how it is verified; per-class facts stay in that class addendum

scope: The next class-subject to be built. Contract 1.6 provisional never went past one pilot and is superseded. Classes 6-9 stay on 1.5 and migrate at import, not by re-issue (D18). Class 10's two tagged pilot units stand at 1.6 and are not re-issued.
supersedes: question_schema_v6 (1.6 provisional) and its amendment log v4 (a1-a13), all folded in
files_carry: "contract_version": "1.7", "schema_file": "<this filename>", "procedure_file": "<the addendum or procedure version built against>"
why_the_split: Contract 1.6 mixed three things in one document: what is stored, what the app mutates, and how to read a PDF. Forty-plus amendment entries were written in three days and almost every one touched the third. The schema had been stable for days inside a document that changed eight times. Splitting them means the schema can be frozen (nobody needs it to change), the procedure can evolve per source, and a unit file can finally say WHICH rules built it — which no 1.5 or 1.6 file can.
what_changed_from_1_6: LOCATORS — every question records where it is printed, source-neutral. The parsers already compute page and y and discard them
STIMULI — a shared passage, table, figure or case serving several questions. Science never needed it; no language paper works without it
RUBRIC answers — criteria-based marking for letters, essays, precis and long-answer source questions
ANSWER EVIDENCE — a verbatim textbook excerpt that may justify an answer. Evidence, never an answer: keys are authored in a reviewed step, never at extraction
ANSWER PROVENANCE — where an answer came from. Without it, root-cause analysis on a wrong answer has nothing to start from
source enum gains teacher and ai; generated and board_qb clarified
pending_category — a question hits a defect category, is tagged, and extraction CONTINUES. Nothing blocks
TEMPLATE type — maths parameterised templates are a different object from a question and had no type at all
Query, Usage, Attempt, WeakItem, MarkResult, KeywordMatching and approval_rules MOVED OUT to the runtime layer

rules.id: Opaque, immutable, deterministic: <subj>-<class>-<chapter2>-s<section1>-q<question3>. section = the source's printed ORDER on the question side (numerals are counted, never read). question = the printed question number, three digits. Un-indexed exercise or practice blocks are segments x1, x2 … in printed order. A question the source leaves unnumbered takes (a) the answer-side number where the key is numbered, recorded in extraction.unnumbered_questions, or (b) -q000, -q000b … by position where no number exists on either side. A DUPLICATED printed number takes a letter suffix by printed order: -q015, -q015b. Chapter membership lives only in chapter_id. Re-runs reproduce identical ids.
rules.id_regex: ^[a-z]{2,4}-(\d{1,2}|puc-[12])-\d{2}-[sx]\d+-q\d{3}[a-z]?$ — the trailing letter admits the duplicate suffix. The 1.6 gate rejected it, which blocked a chapter that the 1.6 rules themselves required it for.
rules.content_hash: SHA-256 hex of normalise(text): NFC (never NFKC); lowercase; fold every Unicode category-Nd character to its ASCII digit; remove every character of category P EXCEPT a '.' or ',' standing between two digits; collapse whitespace; strip. S-category symbols and super/subscript digits are kept. Computed over the corrected text. The same normalisation is used by key_to_option_matching. Computed over `text` ONLY — so correcting an answer never changes a question's identity, and its usage history survives the correction. NOT YET SPECIFIED for Indic scripts or for mathematical notation: lowercasing is meaningless in Kannada and Devanagari, two strings differing only by ZWNJ or a nukta form hash differently, and whitespace collapse makes `2x+3` and `2x + 3` agree while `x^2` and `x²` do not. A normalisation profile is required before any language or maths pilot.
rules.count_gate: The reference is ALWAYS the audited count. audited = highest printed number − gaps + unnumbered + duplicated numbers. reference_source is always 'audited'. quota_table is 'consistent' | 'inconsistent' | 'unparsed' | 'absent' | 'difficulty_only'. second_method is {method, extracted, agrees} and must agree. Practice segments keep a separate tally. Flagged answers count as paired-with-flag.
rules.unit_states: EXTRACTED (count gate passes) → VALIDATED (checklist) → FIGURED (figure identification done; sheet confirmed where any figure exists) → REVIEW-READY (numeric parts classified, notation restored where possible). STOPPED with a stated reason. review_ready is computed from unit_state each build, never hand-set. A unit MAY reach REVIEW-READY carrying pending_category questions; the per-category pending count travels with it. No unit IMPORTS with unresolved pendings.
rules.left_unset_at_extraction: topic_id, out_of_syllabus (false), keyword keys, explanations, accepted_alternates, rubric criteria, difficulty where the source prints none. Set at review or authoring against the Subject Map.

UnitFile.procedure_file: the addendum or procedure version this unit was built against — the field that makes a unit's rules recoverable
UnitFile.amendments_applied: string[] — entries in force at build time
UnitFile.count_gate: {reference, reference_source: 'audited', extracted, paired, flagged, gaps: number[], duplicated_numbers: number[], note?, practice?: {reference, extracted, paired}, quota_table, second_method: {method, extracted, agrees}, pass: boolean}
UnitFile.extraction: {source_file, source_ref_prefix, pdf_pages, printed_page_offset, method_notes: string[], notation_summary: {render_tokens, latex_tokens, damage_flags}, excluded_objects: [{page, w, h, reason, appears_to_be}], inline_excluded_count, unnumbered_questions?, orphan_keys?, inserted_keys? (the two are distinguished by the sequence test — see the port mapping and the procedure layer), unmapped_key_blocks?, verified_shifts?, section_signal?, figure_references?, caveat?}
UnitFile.pending_summary: {<category-id>: count} — computed. Travels with the unit so a large pending set cannot pass unnoticed

Stimulus.text: string — verbatim. For a poem, LINE BREAKS ARE CONTENT and are preserved exactly; they are not whitespace to collapse
Stimulus.note: optional — e.g. the instruction line printed above the block

Locator.source_ref: string — the question's source_ref verbatim: the original filename, never renamed, followed by the question's position (ruled 2026-09-21)
Locator.y: number — top of the block, PDF points, measured DOWN from the page's top edge: the yMin that `pdftotext -bbox-layout` reports. A value measured up from the bottom (PDF's native origin) is wrong and indistinguishable once stored
Locator.block: optional number — paragraph or block ordinal on that page, for a human to find it
Locator.derived_from: 'text_layer' | 'ocr' | 'render_measured' | 'manual' — without this, a coordinate accurate to a point and one accurate to forty look identical, which matters the moment a scanned source is extracted

Question.subject: slug
Question.stimulus_id: optional — names the Stimulus this question is attached to
Question.prior_appearances: optional [{as_printed, exam?, year?}] — the marker is removed from text, so it leaves content_hash
Question.options: optional [{id, text}] for mcq/mcq_multi, or {left:[], right:[]} for match; absent for true_false and yes_no
Question.answer_evidence: optional AnswerEvidence[] — candidate material, NEVER an answer
Question.answer_provenance: AnswerProvenance — REQUIRED whenever an answer is stored (ruled 2026-09-21; gate 2.13 fails without it); absent only on an unanswered question
Question.pending_category: optional string — the defect category this question waits on. The question is flagged, tagged, and extraction CONTINUES; when the category resolves, every question carrying the id is re-processed in one action
Question.locators: Locator[] — REQUIRED, non-empty, where `source` is a printed document (lba | board_qb | mqp | board_paper | textbook): at minimum a role:'question' locator. EMPTY only where `source` is teacher, ai or template (template ruled 2026-09-21: a generated instance is printed nowhere; the template record carries its source), which is what marks a question as having no printed source — no separate boolean is needed. The gate enforces this conditional: without it the field that justifies rendering pages on demand has nothing behind it.
Question.retired_reason: optional — required when status is retired. Retirement never deletes
Question.status_history: [{from,to,by,role,at}] — append-only, and EXTRACTION-TIME ONLY. This file is immutable once tagged, so it records how the question reached its extracted state and stops there. Every later transition — review, an upheld query, a new revision, retirement — lives in the RUNTIME layer keyed by question_id, with `revision` as the join. The trail spans both layers by design: the file is where it starts, the database is where it continues.

AnswerEvidence.text: string — verbatim, stored rather than pointed at, so it survives the source being re-split
AnswerEvidence.note: This is NOT an answer and the generator never renders it. Mode B (textbook-only, no LBA) ships every question with an empty answer, a flag, and the excerpt that may justify one. The authoring pass turns evidence into an answer; extraction that wrote it straight into answer.value would be extraction quietly doing authoring, which the procedure layer forbids.

AnswerProvenance.actor: string — thread id, model id, or person id
AnswerProvenance.brief_version: optional — the authoring brief in force

Asset.caption: optional
Asset.pdf_page: number — the page the object was taken from

Answer.option: {kind:'option', option_id} — mcq (id, or null with a shifted/no-answer flag), true_false ('true'|'false'), yes_no ('yes'|'no'). A yes_no answer may instead be {kind:'text', value} beginning with Yes or No — the full sentence built at authoring (gate 2.12, Yash 2026-09-21); extraction stores the bare printed key
Answer.numeric: {kind:'numeric', parts: [{id, label, value, unit?, tolerance?, accepted_alternates?}]}
Answer.keyword: {kind:'keyword', required, forbidden?, min_required?} — authored at review only
Answer.rubric: {kind:'rubric', criteria: [{id, marks, descriptor}], total_marks} — criteria-based marking for a composition: letters, essays, precis, long-answer source questions. Authored at review. A letter has no key and no keywords; marking it against either was never possible
Answer.text: {kind:'text', value} — human-marked. '[diagram answer — see page image]' plus an asset where the answer is a drawing
Answer.empty: {kind:'text', value:''} with a source_flags entry — the only valid empty

Template.note: A parameterised item, not a Question. Maths ships as templates with constraints and answer formulae; the 1.6 source enum named 'template' while no such type existed.
Template.subject: slug

defect_flag_vocabulary.note: Use the issue text exactly; specifics after an em dash. `suggested` is a proposal, never applied. A category in the defect register keys to one of these strings where one exists; a NEW category means this vocabulary has a gap, which is itself the finding.
defect_flag_vocabulary.key belongs to another paper version: pair only matching keys; others empty + flag
defect_flag_vocabulary.shifted numbering — see key N: EMPTY answer; pointer in suggested; never shift-align
defect_flag_vocabulary.displacement boundary — see key N: the edge of a band; the by-number key may be kept; a content judgement for the reviewer
defect_flag_vocabulary.sub-part labels shifted: extract as printed; flag with suggested
defect_flag_vocabulary.key text paraphrases option: letter valid, wording differs; keep the letter
defect_flag_vocabulary.key text not among options — letter kept: valid letter, text matches no option
defect_flag_vocabulary.key text differs from option by a printe: the printed key and the option differ only by a source typo
defect_flag_vocabulary.key text does not address question: the key answers a different printed question
defect_flag_vocabulary.printed result contradicts working: extract the printed result; suggested carries the arithmetic
defect_flag_vocabulary.no answer printed: no key exists anywhere for this question
defect_flag_vocabulary.answer is a diagram — no key text: NEW. The key is a drawing, not missing. Borrowing 'no answer printed' made eleven faithful extractions across two classes look like defects
defect_flag_vocabulary.duplicate of <id>: identical content_hash within the source; both kept
defect_flag_vocabulary.duplicate stem — keys differ — <id>: NEW. Same stem, different keys. `duplicate of` could say the stems matched but not that the keys conflicted, which was the whole problem. The trailing id names the partner, which must share this question's content_hash; without it the reclassification from `duplicate of <id>` would lose the pointer
defect_flag_vocabulary.no LO mapped: learning_outcomes []; exempt from the suggested expectation
defect_flag_vocabulary.source notation inconsistent — <detail>: extract each occurrence as printed; never harmonise
defect_flag_vocabulary.extraction damage: text-layer notation not restorable per glyph
defect_flag_vocabulary.inline answer pairing ambiguous: a practice block whose layout does not fix the pairing
defect_flag_vocabulary.match key not in pair form: a match key that could not be read as pairs
defect_flag_vocabulary.unclassified — <what is wrong, in a sent: LAST RESORT — only after every entry here AND every category in the defect register was tried. Requires suggested 'nearest: <closest entry | category:<id>> — <why it does not fit>' and pending_category 'unclassified'. Category-pending, not review-blocking: extraction continues. The register row, not this file, records where the instance goes next.
report_level_notes: figure referenced but not printed — <question id>
asset extracts as a single flat colour — <ref>
section heading printed without trailing punctuation — <location>

review_blocking_flags: key text not among options — letter kept
key text does not address question
key text matches several options after normalisation
blocking_note: A flag is review-blocking (the reviewer decides now) or category-pending (it waits on a defect category). They are different states and must not be mixed in one review queue. pending_category distinguishes them.
revisions: 2026-09-21 rev 2 — locators made conditionally required (they were optional, so a thread could ship every one empty and pass); inserted vs orphan disambiguated (1.6 defined both in nearly the same words and 1.7 inherited it); the revision bridge to the runtime layer stated. Revised in place: PROVISIONAL, and no unit file declares 1.7 yet.
2026-09-21 rev 2 — companion reference corrected: it named extraction_procedure_v1, superseded by v2 the same day. Both layer files named the wrong procedure version for several hours.

2026-09-21 rev 3 — `duplicate stem — keys differ` now ends with the partner id (Yash, ratified). The earlier wording carried no pointer, so moving a question off `duplicate of <id>` lost which question it duplicated.

2026-09-21 rev 4 — `unclassified` added as the last-resort entry (Yash); `nearest` may name a register category. Report-level note added for the register's `section-heading-unmatched` category, which had no entry. Before this, a defect fitting no entry could only be forced under a wrong label (silent misclassification) or given an invented one (gate FAIL, blocking the unit the register exists to keep moving).

2026-09-21 rev 5 — Locator.y origin stated: from the top edge, as pdftotext -bbox-layout reports. The field named no origin; PDF's native origin is the bottom, so two correct-looking conventions would have disagreed by the page height.
